title: How four planets share the load when one pin is out of place
question: A helical planetary gear set with four planets runs slowly under torque on a floating sun, with the ring held and the carrier the output. The carrier's hole for planet 1 is out of place along the circumference by the case's error, so that planet 1 leads and is pressed into mesh first. The share of the load each planet carried was measured as the peak tooth-root strain of the ring as it passed, over the sum of the four. Report the mean share of planets 1 and 3 (the diametral pair that the error loads) at the case's sun torque.

conditions.gears: sun 73, planets 26, ring 125 teeth; normal module 1.81 mm; pressure angle 23.04 deg in the source's table, which is the transverse value of a 22.5 deg normal angle at this helix; helix 13.12 deg; operating centre distance 92.12 mm, so the profile shifts sum to x_sun + x_planet = x_ring - x_planet = +0.0685 (their split is not stated); face width 25 mm; all ground, with small planet tooth-thickness and run-out errors; the planets' outside diameters reduced slightly (by an amount not stated); no profile or lead modification stated
conditions.assembly: four planets at 0, 90.91, 180 and 270.91 deg (multiples of 360 / 198 deg: 198 / 4 is not whole), numbered counter-clockwise from planet 1; each planet on needle bearings on a pin in the carrier; the sun floating (a three-planet test with a large error gave equal shares); the ring a thick one (rim 13 mm below the roots) held by 11 external splines, 32.7 deg apart, in an adaptor in which it floats radially to some extent
conditions.error: a tangential position error of planet 1's carrier hole only, positive when planet 1 leads into mesh and carries more (the source's clockwise tests); the actual hole positions were not measured
conditions.operation: a power-recirculating rig with an identical reaction set; the sun at 500 rpm; automatic transmission fluid at room temperature; 26 carrier rotations (the hunting period) averaged in each of three segments
conditions.measurement: foil strain gauges in the ring's tooth roots (groups of three consecutive roots about the ring); each planet's share L_i is its peak root strain as it passes over the sum of the four (the shares sum to 1, 1/4 each when equal); the output is (L_1 + L_3) / 2
conditions.not_stated: tip and root diameters, the split of the profile shifts, the material (steel), the planets' needle-bearing stiffness (two published models of this rig used 2e5 N/mm and 1.3e5 N/mm), the carrier's and pins' compliance, the splines' geometry and clearance, the gauges' exact place in the root

outputs.name: overloaded_pair_share
outputs.meaning: (L_1 + L_3) / 2: the mean share of planet 1 and planet 3, from the ring's root strain

practice.note: the same carrier run the other way, so planet 1 lags and carries less: (L_1 + L_3) / 2 = 0.171 measured (L_2 and L_4 carry 0.331); public so that an entrant can check the sign and the reduction, not tune the physics

label: T6
subtitle: Leads to flag 06 · four helical planets, one pin out of place, load sharing from the ring's root strain
